item.title: Chinese relief supplies arrive in Nepal
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
Staff members prepare to unload Chinese relief supplies at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, Nepal, Aug. 30, 2026. Carried by two Y-20 transport planes, Chinese relief supplies and four Chinese rescue experts arrived here at about 7 a.m. local time on Sunday to assist in disaster relief efforts. The mudslides, which hit Nepal on Wednesday, have caused heavy casualties and widespread damage to infrastructure. (Xinhua/Zhang Ping) KATHMANDU, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- Carried by two Y-20 transport planes, Chinese relief supplies and four Chinese rescue experts arrived at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, Nepal, at about 7 a.m. local time on Sunday to assist in disaster relief efforts. The two aircraft departed from Chengdu, China, earlier in the morning and arrived in Nepal after a flight of about three hours. The relief supplies, including tents, blankets, sleeping bags, hardtack and emergency kits, were handed over to the Nepali side at the airport. Chinese Ambassador to Nepal Zhang Maoming and Nepal's Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation Mahabir Pun attended the handover ceremony. The mudslides, which hit Nepal on Wednesday, have caused heavy casualties and widespread damage to infrastructure. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said that 734 bodies had been recovered from mudslide-hit areas as of 9 a.m. local time on Sunday, with 2,498 people still missing. ■ Staff members prepare to unload Chinese relief supplies at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, Nepal, Aug. 30, 2026. item.title: Factbox: Latest relief and rescue progress at mudslide-hit border port in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
A press conference is held by the information office of the Xizang regional government to brief the rescue and relief efforts after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in the autonomous region, in Xigaze, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Aug. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Tenzing Nima Qadhup) BEIJING, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse on the Nepali side, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, causing heavy casualties and leaving many missing. Chinese rescuers immediately launched an all-out effort to reach the mudslide-hit port area and search for the missing. Here is what we know about the deadly mudslide and the latest rescue and relief progress there: -- Sixteen people have been confirmed dead and 546 others remain missing as of 6 p.m. Saturday, according to the regional government. -- A total of 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries have been identified as unaccounted for after the mudslide. The figure was announced on Sunday morning at a press conference held by the information office of the regional government, following a joint search and cross-checking of information by foreign affairs, public security, culture and tourism, and emergency management authorities. -- During his phone conversation with Nepali Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal on Saturday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said that China attaches great importance to the disaster, which also caused heavy casualties and left many missing in Nepal. Wang said that while urgently carrying out rescue and relief efforts on its own side, China extended a helping hand at the earliest opportunity and supported Nepal in its emergency disaster relief efforts. -- A total of 2,141 Chinese rescuers have joined the mission, according to the update by the region's emergency management department on early Saturday morning. Excavators were busy repairing a key road to facilitate entry into the port. A total length of 2.6 km of road section had been restored, leaving 1.7 kilometers to go before reaching Gyirong Port by around 1 p.m. Saturday. -- All civilian vehicles and personnel are prohibited from traveling toward Gyirong Township, with immediate effect, according to a notice issued on Saturday by the local traffic police. The notice specified that only authorized special-purpose vehicles for emergency rescue, disaster relief, and material support are permitted to pass with valid permits. The restrictions will remain in place until further notice. -- China's Ministry of Emergency Management on Saturday dispatched five Chinese tunnel experts to Nepal to support rescue efforts at a hydropower plant tunnel, at the request of the Nepali government. -- Three sets of portable automatic weather stations have been deployed to provide targeted weather support for restoring road access, search and rescue operations, drone flights and surveying a barrier lake, the China Meteorological Administration said Saturday. -- The National Cryosphere Desert Data Center has provided 53 service datasets, with a total data volume of roughly 85 GB, available for download and use by relevant emergency response, rescue and research institutions. -- The National Earth Observation Data Center has compiled remote sensing data resources from civilian and commercial satellites, with a total data volume exceeding 20 GB. The data is provided to support post-disaster road damage assessment, building collapse identification, and secondary disaster monitoring. ■ A press conference is held by the information office of the Xizang regional government to brief the rescue and relief efforts after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in the autonomous region, in Xigaze, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Aug. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Tenzing Nima Qadhup)

item.title: Ice-rock avalanche in Nepal triggers deadly mudslide in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- An ice-rock avalanche originating from a high-mountain glacier in Nepal has been identified as the cause of a devastating mudslide that struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, local authorities said Sunday. A glacier on the south slope of Mount Langtang Lirung in Nepal fractured at an altitude of about 5,200 meters, triggering an ice-rock avalanche, according to a press conference held by the information office of the regional government. The avalanche plunged rapidly to an altitude of around 4,000 meters, scouring the mountainside and developing into a massive debris flow, which surged about 22 kilometers before reaching Gyirong Port at an altitude of around 1,800 meters. The disaster flattened an area of about 0.7 square kilometers, destroying 27 buildings and related facilities in the area. The findings were made by a cryosphere emergency disaster response team from the Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, based on the analysis of remote-sensing monitoring data and field-transmitted data, as well as on-site surveys and investigations. The deadly mudslide had claimed 16 lives and left 546 others missing at Gyirong Port as of 6 p.m. Saturday, the regional government said on Sunday morning. Su Pengcheng, a researcher with the institute, said the disaster is the result of glacier instability under the long-term effects of climate warming. A post-disaster investigation found that the narrow valley and steep vertical drop in the area where the ice-rock avalanche occurred gave the collapsing mass enormous potential energy. As it descended rapidly, friction and impacts generated large amounts of heat and meltwater. The resulting mixture swept up moraine and other loose material along the valley and rapidly developed into a debris flow. It reached Gyirong Port at around 10:59 a.m. on Aug. 26, only six to seven minutes after the initial collapse, Su said. The debris flow caused blockage and backwater near the port before continuing downstream into Nepal. Su said the disaster was marked by its sudden onset, large peak flow, high speed, strong destructive force and wide impact area, characteristics that he described as a notable new feature of cryospheric disasters on and around the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Meanwhile, a barrier dam above the core area of Gyirong Port is currently stable and unlikely to suffer a sudden complete breach, according to the press conference. Radar monitoring showed that the dam has an average height of 60 meters and a length of about 1,100 meters. The lake behind it covers about 0.1 square kilometers and has a storage capacity of around 2.2 million cubic meters. Authorities said that the dam has begun discharging water through overflow and is generally stable. Rescue operations remain difficult because of the high-altitude terrain, steep valleys and volatile weather, while the surrounding area still faces potential risks from glaciers, glacial lakes and geological hazards, Su said. So far, a total of 2,141 personnel have joined search and rescue operations, including personnel from the People's Liberation Army, the People's Armed Police Force, the China Search and Rescue Team, China Anneng, border defense units and police, according to the press conference. A total of 269 rescue vehicles and 3,922 sets of rescue equipment have also been dispatched to the front line, where rescue teams have searched an area of 90,000 square meters. ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: How the SCO is raising the bar for better global governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
BEIJING, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- The world is facing a growing crisis of global governance. Protectionism, unilateralism and power politics are throttling international cooperation just as mounting global challenges demand it most. Against this backdrop, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at last year's "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" Meeting, calling for a more just and equitable system of global governance. The SCO offers a practical answer. Over the past 25 years, it has demonstrated how countries with different political systems, development paths and civilizations can work together. Guided by the Shanghai Spirit of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity of civilizations and pursuit of common development, the SCO's 25-year practice offers a vivid illustration of the five principles of the Global Governance Initiative -- adhering to sovereign equality, abiding by international rule of law, practicing multilateralism, advocating the people-centered approach, and focusing on taking real actions. These principles are reflected in the SCO's increasingly institutionalized cooperation across a wide range of sectors. With regional security and stability at the heart of its original mission, SCO countries have committed themselves to long-term good neighborliness, friendship and cooperation based on equality, consultation and respect for diversity. The establishment of four new security-focused centers demonstrated the SCO's emphasis on translating multilateral consensus into concrete action. Cooperation among SCO countries has helped thwart more than 1,400 terrorism- and extremism-related incidents in the past 25 years, while the organization has conducted over 40 joint counter-terrorism exercises and operations. The SCO's approach to security also reflects a broader understanding among SCO countries that lasting security cannot be separated from political trust, economic development and people-to-people exchanges. The launch of seven China-SCO cooperation platforms covering green industry, digital economy, scientific and technological innovation, energy, higher education, vocational and technical education, and artificial intelligence further underscores the emphasis on shared development with people-centered outcomes. Through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and closer alignment of development strategies, SCO members have seen positive momentum in both foreign trade and intra-SCO commerce. Calculations based on World Trade Organization data showed the total volume of goods imports and exports of the ten members reached about 8.88 trillion U.S. dollars in 2025. Projects such as the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, the Silk Road e-commerce service hub and the SCO university network are further turning connectivity into tangible benefits, making it easier for people across SCO countries to travel, trade, study and access broader economic opportunities. People-to-people exchange activities have also become an important pillar of SCO cooperation. Through institutionalized dialogue and expanded interaction, differences in history, culture and civilization can be turned into sources of mutual understanding and cooperation. Beyond the region, the SCO has played an active role in upholding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and international law, contributing to the settlement of regional and international issues and promoting coordination among multilateral mechanisms. The SCO Plus format has further broadened the space for dialogue among the Global South, facilitating exchanges in governance experience and practical cooperation. Over the past decades, the SCO has shown that diversity need not lead to division, and that countries with different political systems, development paths, and civilizations can cooperate on equal footing without butting heads. Looking ahead, the SCO is well positioned to bolster high-quality regional development and contribute more wisdom to building a more just and equitable global governance system.■
